about: The contract of the Node rows bridge: the one door the Rust host uses to reach the doctor rows and fixes whose layers Node still owns (owner bridge:<step> in doctor-registry.v1.json). The host starts `module` of the legacy payload with the payload's Node, writes one request as JSON on its stdin and reads one line per result from its stdout. Only a line that starts with resultPrefix is a result, so output a body prints can never be read as one; each result is written as soon as it exists, so a crash keeps what was produced; the call ends with one `end` line carrying the number of results and, optionally, `nodeVersion` (the `process.version` of the Node that ran the call, which the host judges against the release's `requires.node` instead of starting a Node of its own), and a call without it did not finish. A malformed request or an id with no body is one `refusal` line. One more request shares the door until the Work layer moves: `work-store-init` creates the Work store of the project's `.fgos` (the Event Store rebuild `fgos init` needs); it has no ids, answers with an `end` line of count 0 when it worked, and with a `refusal` line whose optional `category` is the error's exit category when it did not. The level of a row (`status` when the row does not say it), the fix of a failing row, `ok` and `next` are the host's, never the bridge's. Each side reads `vectors`: the Node module writes exactly `line` for `kind` and `body`, the host reads `line` back as `body`. The bridge ends with the last Node-owned row.

request.phase: `fix` (every id is a fix id), `check` (every id is a row id) or `work-store-init` (no ids)
request.ids: a non-empty-string id each, in registry order; one call per run of consecutive fixes of the bridge, one call for every bridged row; an empty list for `work-store-init`
request.dir: the project root the run acts on (for `work-store-init`, the project whose `.fgos` the store is created in)

vectors.name: a judged row with everything it can say
vectors.line: FGOS-DOCTOR-BRIDGE {"kind":"row","id":"curl-available","passed":false,"status":"fail","message":"curl is not on PATH","fixCommand":"install curl","detail":{"path":"/usr/bin"}}
